question_text: The mean of a set of 50 numbers is 6, and the mean of another set of $n$ numbers is 9. The mean of the combined sets of $50 + n$ numbers is 8. Find the value of $n$.
solution:
Convert each mean into a total.
$$\text{Total of the first set}=50\times 6=300$$
$$\text{Total of the second set}=n\times 9=9n$$
The combined set has $50+n$ numbers and mean 8, so
$$\frac{300+9n}{50+n}=8$$
$$300+9n=8(50+n)=400+8n$$
$$9n-8n=400-300$$
$$n=100$$

question_text: As part of the inter-disciplinary unit, many groups have mooted the idea of implementing vertical gardening for food sustainability in the school. The diagram below shows a recommendation of how the auto-irrigation system for the plants may look like. The container is in the form of a right hollow cone joined to a cylinder. The diameter of the cylinder is 42 cm and the height of the cone is 20 cm. 25 000 cm$^3$ of water is poured into it. [Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$] (Curved surface area of cone $= \pi r l$, Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h$)

parts.text: Calculate the height of the water in the cylinder, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Radius $= \frac{42}{2} = 21$ cm
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^{2} \times 20 = 9240$ cm$^3$
The cone fills first, so the volume of water in the cylinder $= 25000 - 9240 = 15760$ cm$^3$
Cross-sectional area of cylinder $= \frac{22}{7} \times 21^{2} = 1386$ cm$^2$
Height of water in the cylinder $= \frac{15760}{1386} = 11.3708\ldots$
Height $= 11.4$ cm (3 s.f.)

parts.text: Given that the slant height of the cone is 29 cm, calculate the surface area of the container that is in contact with the water, giving your answer correct to the nearest ten.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The water touches the whole curved surface of the cone and the curved surface of the cylinder up to the water level.
Curved surface area of cone $= \pi r l = \frac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 29 = 1914$ cm$^2$
Curved surface area of the wetted cylinder $= 2\pi r h = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 11.3708\ldots = 1500.95\ldots$ cm$^2$
Total $= 1914 + 1500.95 = 3414.95\ldots$ cm$^2$
Surface area $= 3410$ cm$^2$ (to the nearest ten)

parts.text: It is recommended that the water system be programmed to water the plants once a day in the morning, dispensing 3000 cm$^3$ of water each time. The container will be refilled with 25 000 cm$^3$ of water in the evening when it contains less than 1200 cm$^3$ of water. If the container is first filled with water on a Sunday evening, write down and explain when the next time water must be topped up.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: On the Monday evening of the following week, because after the 8th watering only $1000$ cm$^3$ is left, which is less than $1200$ cm$^3$.
parts.solution:
The container starts with $25000$ cm$^3$ and loses $3000$ cm$^3$ each morning.
After $n$ waterings the container holds $(25000 - 3000n)$ cm$^3$.
After 7 waterings: $25000 - 21000 = 4000$ cm$^3$, which is not less than $1200$ cm$^3$, so no refill.
After 8 waterings: $25000 - 24000 = 1000$ cm$^3$, which is less than $1200$ cm$^3$, so it must be refilled.
The first watering is on Monday morning, so the 8th watering is on the Monday of the following week.
Water must be topped up on that Monday evening, 8 days after the first filling.

question_text: A small pipe takes $x$ minutes to fill a tank while a large pipe takes $y$ minutes to fill the same tank. Express as a single fraction, in terms of $x$ and $y$, the time taken to fill the tank if both pipes were switched on.
solution:
In 1 minute the small pipe fills $\dfrac{1}{x}$ of the tank.
In 1 minute the large pipe fills $\dfrac{1}{y}$ of the tank.
Together, in 1 minute they fill $\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y} = \dfrac{y + x}{xy}$ of the tank.
Time taken to fill the whole tank $= 1 \div \dfrac{x + y}{xy}$
$= \dfrac{xy}{x + y}$ minutes

question_text:
The daily Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) reading at 8 am for Singapore from 19 to 30 June 2013 is shown below.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline 105 & 173 & 198 & 246 & 128 & 96 \\ \hline 77 & 61 & 59 & 62 & 62 & 70 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.text: Find the median PSI.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Arrange the $12$ readings in ascending order:
$59, 61, 62, 62, 70, 77, 96, 105, 128, 173, 198, 246$
Since $n = 12$ is even, the median is the mean of the $6$th and $7$th values.
$6$th value $= 77$, $7$th value $= 96$
Median $= \frac{77 + 96}{2} = \frac{173}{2} = 86.5$

parts.text:
The information above is shown in the following grouped frequency table.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \text{PSI, } x & \text{Frequency} \\ \hline 50 < x \leq 100 & 7 \\ \hline 100 < x \leq 150 & 2 \\ \hline 150 < x \leq 200 & 2 \\ \hline 200 < x \leq 250 & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
parts.label: b

subparts.text: On the grid below, draw a histogram to represent the data.
subparts.label: i
subparts.answer: Bars of height $7$, $2$, $2$, $1$ over $50 < x \leq 100$, $100 < x \leq 150$, $150 < x \leq 200$, $200 < x \leq 250$, drawn adjacent with no gaps.
subparts.solution:
All four class intervals have equal width $50$, so the height of each bar is simply the frequency.
Draw bars with PSI on the horizontal axis and frequency on the vertical axis:
$50 < x \leq 100$: height $7$
$100 < x \leq 150$: height $2$
$150 < x \leq 200$: height $2$
$200 < x \leq 250$: height $1$
The bars must touch one another with no gaps, because the data is continuous and grouped into adjoining intervals.

subparts.text: Find an estimate of the mean PSI.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
Use the mid-value of each class interval to estimate the mean.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Mid-value } x & \text{Frequency } f & fx \\ \hline 75 & 7 & 525 \\ \hline 125 & 2 & 250 \\ \hline 175 & 2 & 350 \\ \hline 225 & 1 & 225 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Mean $= \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$
$= \frac{525 + 250 + 350 + 225}{7 + 2 + 2 + 1}$
$= \frac{1350}{12}$
$= 112.5$

subparts.text: State the modal class.
subparts.label: iii
subparts.solution:
The modal class is the class interval with the highest frequency.
The frequencies are $7$, $2$, $2$ and $1$, so the highest frequency is $7$.
Modal class $= 50 < x \leq 100$

answer: Median PSI $= 86.5$; mean PSI $= 112.5$; modal class $50 < x \leq 100$

question_text: The diagram shows an inverted right pyramid, $VABCD$, with a hole in the shape of a hemisphere removed from the top. $ABCD$ is a square of side 14 cm and $VE = 21.2$ cm. Radius of the hemisphere is 3 cm.

parts.text: Calculate the total exposed surface area of the solid. Give your answer to one significant figure.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
The exposed surface is made up of three parts: the four slanting triangular faces, the square top with the circular hole removed, and the curved surface of the hemispherical hole.
Four triangular faces (base $14$ cm, slant height $VE = 21.2$ cm):
$4 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 21.2 = 593.6$ cm$^{2}$
Square top less the circle of radius $3$ cm:
$14^{2} - \pi(3)^{2} = 196 - 28.274 = 167.726$ cm$^{2}$
Curved surface of the hemisphere:
$2\pi r^{2} = 2\pi(3)^{2} = 56.549$ cm$^{2}$
Total exposed surface area
$= 593.6 + 167.726 + 56.549$
$= 817.875$ cm$^{2}$
$= 800$ cm$^{2}$ (1 s.f.)

Volume of a hemisphere $= \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$= \frac{2}{3}\pi (3)^{3}$
$= \frac{2}{3}\pi \times 27$
$= 18\pi$ cm$^{3}$

In Fit Bit Secondary School, students with a Body Mass Index (BMI) of more than 23.5 have to attend fitness training every Friday morning before lessons begin. In January 2018, Jing Hua's height was $164$ cm and his weight was $M$ kg. If he was not required to attend the fitness training in the first half of the year, find the greatest possible integer value of $M$.
$$\left\lbrack BMI = \frac{\text{weight}}{(\text{height})^2}, \text{ where weight is in kg and height is in metres.} \right\rbrack$$
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Height $= 164$ cm $= 1.64$ m
He is not required to attend, so BMI $\le 23.5$:
$\frac{M}{1.64^2} \le 23.5$
$M \le 23.5 \times 2.6896$
$M \le 63.2056$
Greatest possible integer value of $M = 63$

parts.text: In July 2018, Jing Hua's height increased by $1\%$ and his weight increased by $4\%$. Would Jing Hua have to attend the Friday fitness training for the second half of the year? Show your working clearly using the greatest possible integer value of $M$ obtained in part (a) as Jing Hua's original weight.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Yes. New BMI $= 23.9 > 23.5$, so he has to attend the fitness training.
parts.solution:
New height $= 1.64 \times 1.01 = 1.6564$ m
New weight $= 63 \times 1.04 = 65.52$ kg
New BMI $= \frac{65.52}{1.6564^2} = \frac{65.52}{2.74366} = 23.880$
Since $23.880 > 23.5$, Jing Hua has to attend the Friday fitness training.

parts.text: The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 141. Find the biggest number.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
Let the numbers be $x$, $x + 2$ and $x + 4$.
$3x + 6 = 141$
$3x = 135$
$x = 45$
The numbers are 45, 47 and 49, so the biggest number is 49.

parts.text: The sum of the ages of Cindy and her sister is 38. Seven years ago, Cindy was thrice as old as her sister. Find Cindy's age now.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Let Cindy be $x$ years old now; her sister is $(38 - x)$ years old.
$x - 7 = 3[(38 - x) - 7]$
$x - 7 = 3(31 - x) = 93 - 3x$
$4x = 100$
$x = 25$
Cindy is 25 years old now.

parts.text: It is given that $x$ and $y$ are integers such that $0 \le x \le 7$ and $0 \le y \le 4$. Calculate the greatest value of $x - 2y$.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
$x - 2y$ is greatest when $x$ is as large as possible and $2y$ is as small as possible.
Largest $x = 7$; smallest $y = 0$.
Greatest value $= 7 - 2(0) = 7$

parts.text: A series of three light bulbs switch on every 15, 32 and 48 seconds respectively. Given that they lit up together at 6 am, when is the next time all the three light bulbs will light up together again?
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
The bulbs light up together again after the LCM of 15, 32 and 48 seconds.
$15 = 3 \times 5$
$32 = 2^{5}$
$48 = 2^{4} \times 3$
LCM $= 2^{5} \times 3 \times 5 = 480$ seconds $= 8$ minutes
Next time $= 6.00\text{ am} + 8\text{ min} = 6.08\text{ am}$

parts.text: Given that $200 = 2^{3} \times 5^{2}$, it is stated that $200k$ is both a perfect square and a perfect cube. Find the smallest possible value of $k$.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
A number that is both a perfect square and a perfect cube is a perfect sixth power, so every index in $200k$ must be a multiple of $6$.
$200k = 2^{3} \times 5^{2} \times k$
Raise the index of $2$ from $3$ to $6$ and the index of $5$ from $2$ to $6$:
$k = 2^{3} \times 5^{4} = 8 \times 625 = 5000$
Check: $200 \times 5000 = 1\,000\,000 = 1000^{2} = 100^{3}$ ✓

question_text:
The following tables show the climatic data of two cities in South America.
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Jan} & \text{Feb} & \text{Mar} & \text{Apr} & \text{May} & \text{June} & \text{July} & \text{Aug} & \text{Sep} & \text{Oct} & \text{Nov} & \text{Dec} \\ \hline \text{Temp } (^\circ\text{C}) & 26 & 27 & 26 & 25 & 23 & 22 & 21 & 22 & 22 & 23 & 24 & 25 \\ \hline \text{Precipitation (mm)} & 114 & 105 & 103 & 137 & 86 & 80 & 56 & 51 & 87 & a & 96 & 169 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Ushuaia, Argentina:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Jan} & \text{Feb} & \text{Mar} & \text{Apr} & \text{May} & \text{June} & \text{July} & \text{Aug} & \text{Sep} & \text{Oct} & \text{Nov} & \text{Dec} \\ \hline \text{Temp } (^\circ\text{C}) & 10 & 10 & 8 & 6 & 3 & 1 & b & c & 4 & 6 & 8 & 9 \\ \hline \text{Precipitation (mm)} & 40 & 30 & 30 & 40 & 30 & 40 & 30 & 30 & 20 & 30 & 20 & 30 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.text: Find the annual mean temperature for Rio de Janeiro.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
Sum of the 12 temperatures $= 26 + 27 + 26 + 25 + 23 + 22 + 21 + 22 + 22 + 23 + 24 + 25 = 286$
Mean $= \frac{286}{12} = 23.833\ldots$
Annual mean temperature $= 23.8^\circ$C (3 s.f.)

parts.text: If the median precipitation for Rio de Janeiro is 92 mm, find the value of $a$.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
There are 12 values, so the median is the mean of the 6th and 7th values when they are arranged in order.
The 11 known values in order are $51, 56, 80, 86, 87, 96, 103, 105, 114, 137, 169$.
Since the median is 92, $a$ must lie between 87 and 96, giving the order
$51, 56, 80, 86, 87, a, 96, 103, 105, 114, 137, 169$.
$\frac{a + 96}{2} = 92$
$a + 96 = 184$
$a = 88$, which does lie between 87 and 96.

parts.text: Given that the annual mean temperature of Ushuaia is $5.75^\circ$C, find the value of $b$ and of $c$, given that the coldest month is in June and there are four modal temperatures for the year.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Total of the 12 temperatures $= 5.75 \times 12 = 69$
Sum of the ten known temperatures $= 10 + 10 + 8 + 6 + 3 + 1 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 9 = 65$
So $b + c = 69 - 65 = 4$.
June is the coldest month at $1^\circ$C, so $b > 1$ and $c > 1$.
The only whole numbers greater than 1 adding to 4 are $b = 2$ and $c = 2$.
Check: the temperatures are $10, 10, 8, 6, 3, 1, 2, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9$, so $2$, $6$, $8$ and $10$ each occur twice, giving four modal temperatures.

parts.text: With reference to the two tables, make 2 comparisons, 1 using the data on temperature and 1 using the data on precipitation, about the climate of Rio de Janeiro and Ushuaia.
parts.label: d
parts.answer: Temperature: Rio de Janeiro is much warmer, with an annual mean of $23.8^\circ$C compared with $5.75^\circ$C for Ushuaia. Precipitation: Rio de Janeiro is much wetter, receiving between 51 mm and 169 mm each month compared with only 20 mm to 40 mm for Ushuaia.
parts.solution:
Temperature: the annual mean temperature of Rio de Janeiro is $23.8^\circ$C, which is about four times the annual mean of $5.75^\circ$C for Ushuaia, so Rio de Janeiro is much warmer all year round. Rio de Janeiro also has a smaller temperature range ($27 - 21 = 6^\circ$C) than Ushuaia ($10 - 1 = 9^\circ$C), so its temperature is more consistent.
Precipitation: Rio de Janeiro receives far more rain every month (from 51 mm to 169 mm) than Ushuaia (from 20 mm to 40 mm), so Rio de Janeiro is much wetter. Rio de Janeiro's monthly precipitation also varies a great deal, whereas Ushuaia's stays close to 30 mm throughout the year.

answer: (a) $23.8^\circ$C; (b) $a = 88$; (c) $b = 2$, $c = 2$; (d) Temperature: Rio de Janeiro is much warmer, with an annual mean of $23.8^\circ$C compared with $5.75^\circ$C for Ushuaia. Precipitation: Rio de Janeiro is much wetter, receiving between 51 mm and 169 mm each month compared with only 20 mm to 40 mm for Ushuaia.
